notes:
Topline: Umbrage is a regulated fintech providing escrow and custody services across EU and UK. They require a Private (VPC) deployment with strong audit logging to feed their central SIEM (Splunk/Elastic), CMEK for all logs, and data residency locked to eu-west-1. Deal is in procurement; legal and SecOps are the gating groups.

Recent timeline:
- 2026-01-15: Intro call (AE M. Chen, SE R. Patel). High level requirements captured: VPC-only, CMEK, 7+ year retention for audit events, real-time SIEM export.
- 2026-02-04: Security questionnaire submitted (attached). Awaiting DPA redlines.
- 2026-02-24: Deep-dive with SecOps (fireflies ff-2026-02-24-umbrage-sr). Walked through log types and SIEM ingestion options.
- 2026-03-09: Internal SIEM mapping workshop (fireflies ff-2026-03-09-siem-workshop). Customer demo request for PoC ingestion.
- 2026-03-10: Follow-up with Legal re: CMEK access pattern and SOW.

Audit logging / SIEM requirements (customer-specified):
- Destination: primary requirement is push to customer-managed Splunk HEC endpoint in eu region, fallback to S3 (encrypted) + Kinesis Firehose. Elastic ingestion also acceptable via Kafka connector.
- Protocols / transports supported: HTTPS POST to HEC, syslog/CEF over TLS, S3 batch export (parquet/json), Kafka topic with TLS mutual auth. Must support TLS 1.2+ and client cert mTLS for push.
- Log schema (must include the following fields; schema versioning required):
    * timestamp (ISO8601 UTC)
    * request_id (uuid)
    * account_id / tenant_id
    * user_id / service_account
    * model_id and model_variant
    * operation_type (chat/generate/embedding/rerank)
    * prompt_hash (sha256) - customer requires hashed prompts for matching without storing raw PII
    * token_in, token_out counts
    * latency_ms and stage_breakdowns (kv_cache_hit, batching_delay)
    * response_status and error_code
    * fallback_event (true/false) + fallback_reason
    * client_ip (anonymize if PII policy requires)
    * kms_key_id (CMEK identifier) and encryption_metadata
    * audit_action (create/read/update/delete/config_change)
    * actor_role and actor_origin (console/api/sdk)
- Access logs: HTTP access logs for all control-plane interactions (console/API) must be exported and correlated with request logs. Must include subject (user/service), method, route, response_code, bytes_in/out.
- Retention and tiering: Primary requirement: immutable retention policy of 7 years for "security-audit" index; ability to set shorter retention (90/365 days) for non-audit logs. Hot storage for 90 days, cold for remainder. Customer requires WORM-style retention support or legal hold.
- Encryption & key management: All logs at rest must be encrypted with customer-managed keys (CMEK/HSM). KMS integration pattern must allow: key creation by customer or grant-access model, key rotation policy, and audit trail of key usage. Must provide instructions for secure key binding during PoC.
- PII controls & redaction: Must support configurable redaction rules (regex, JSON path), on-the-fly masking, and sampled raw payload capture for debug (by request only and with elevated access). Customer wants hashed prompt storage by default.
- Throughput & SLAs: Real-time export target of sub-5s delivery to Splunk HEC at 500 req/s sustained for PoC traffic profile; support burst to 2k req/s.
- Observability & auditability: Schema version field and field-level hashes for non-repudiation. Ability to produce signed daily manifests of exported batches (S3) for integrity verification.
- Change control: Any schema change must go through a 30-day notice + migration plan.

Recommended Redwood PoC / deliverables (agreed in meeting):
- Deliver sample JSON audit-log schema doc and 48-hour streaming demo to customer Splunk HEC in eu-west-1.
- Provide architecture diagram for CMEK integration and roles/permissions required.
- Wire up S3 export + Kinesis Firehose fallback in PoC. Provide sample queries for SecOps dashboards.
- Run retention policy test (simulate legal hold and deleted record request).

Questions / open technical items called out by SecOps:
- Can Redwood guarantee that raw prompts will never be stored in plaintext in logs? (answer: will provide hashed prompt option + sampling controls; details in security FAQ).
- What is the exact contract path for granting Redwood access to CMEK keys? They want a model that avoids Redwood key export.
- Need to confirm Splunk HEC throughput and mTLS certificate rotation process.
- Legal: DPA redlines on subprocessing / residency.

Sales notes (AE/SE):
- Customer values clear control plane separation and audit provenance; good fit for Private with VPC peering + dedicated networking.
- Pricing ask: want committed capacity for 24/7 low-latency chat endpoints and separate billing for long-term log retention (hot/cold).
- Close plan: get SecOps PO for PoC by 2026-04; legal to finish DPA by 2026-05; aim to sign Dedicated/Private contract by 2026-06.

Next steps (concrete):
1) Deliver SIEM schema v0.1 + sample payloads (SE R. Patel) — due 2026-03-16.
2) Book mapping workshop with customer Splunk engineer (AE to schedule) — target 2026-03-22.
3) Draft PoC SOW including CMEK binding steps and retention tests (legal & solutions) — draft by 2026-03-26.

Stubs / references: security FAQ (drive link), PoC SOW draft, INF-9912 ticket for export pipeline.

Representative quotes: "We need the logs to look like other platform events — same fields, same retention logic. No surprises during audits." — Umbrage SecOps lead

CRM shorthand: high-signal enterprise, strong chance if SecOps PoC passes. Key risk = DPA/CMEK legal friction.
